blocks.heading: Your site exists. Google ignores it.

items.text: Your site exists. Google ignores it.

A familiar picture: the website looks fine, but brings almost no search traffic. Some pages are not indexed, titles are duplicated, the site is slow on mobile, and the texts do not match what people actually type into Google. Each page tries to rank for everything and ends up ranking for nothing.

SEO fixes this step by step: technical problems first, then structure and keywords, then content and links. It is slower than ads, but the traffic does not vanish the moment you pause a budget. That is why we combine SEO with paid ads when a business needs enquiries now.

A technical and on-page check: indexing, crawl errors, speed and Core Web Vitals, mobile version, duplicates, meta tags and structured data. You get a prioritised list of fixes you can hand to any developer.
Indexing · Core Web Vitals · Structured data
We collect search queries for your languages and markets, group them by intent and map each group to one page. Missing pages go into a content plan.
Titles, headings, internal links and texts written for people first. We improve existing pages and create new ones only where there is real search demand.
Google Business Profile, categories, photos, a process for collecting reviews, consistent name, address and phone across listings, and local landing pages for each city or branch.
Google Business Profile · Google Maps · Local pages
Careful, relevant links: industry directories, partner sites, guest articles. No link farms or schemes that put your site at risk of penalties.
A short report based on Google Search Console and GA4: impressions, clicks, pages that grew or dropped, what we did and what comes next.
Technical audit of the site and a look at competitors in your niche.
Keyword map, priorities and a content plan for the next months.
Technical fixes, page optimisation, first new pages.
New content, links, wider keyword coverage, monthly review.

items.q: How long does SEO take to show results?
items.a: Usually 3–6 months for the first noticeable results. It depends on competition, the age of the site and how many technical issues need fixing first.

items.q: How much do your SEO services cost?
items.a: SEO starts from $150/month. A basic audit is from $100 (up to 50 pages, 3 days), a full audit from $300 (5 days). Local SEO starts from $200 one-off, $150/month for one location or $400/month for a network of branches.
No, and be careful with anyone who does. Google's algorithms and your competitors change all the time. We commit to a clear plan, monthly work you can check, and reports based on Search Console data.

items.q: Should I start with an audit or monthly SEO?
items.a: If you are not sure what is wrong with the site, start with an audit. It gives a list of fixes your own developer can implement. Monthly SEO makes sense when you want us to do the work and keep growing the site.

items.q: Can you do SEO for sites in German, Polish or English?
items.a: Yes. Keyword research is done separately for each language and country. Texts in a language we do not write natively should be reviewed by a native speaker — on your side or a translator you trust.

items.q: What do you need from us?
items.a: Access to the website admin or code, Google Search Console and GA4. If they are not set up yet, we set them up at the start.

items.q: Is local SEO worth it for a small business?
items.a: If your customers come from one city or area — a clinic, a salon, a repair service, a restaurant — Google Maps is often where they find you. A complete, active Google Business Profile is one of the most practical things to fix first.
